analysis.title: SpaceXonomics: 10 Thoughts in 10 Bullets
key_insights: Market reaction to a near flawless Starship Flight 15 and historic ship catch was muted. MS says investors see SPCX as combining uncertainty in business model (AI/neocloud), customer concentration and strategy (Tesla).
Incoming SPCX call volume on the day of the catch was among the quietest in weeks.

Cybercab ordering is invite-only and limited to Austin, Dallas, Houston, Fort Worth, San Antonio, Miami, Orlando and Tampa. MS views delivering a no-steering-wheel car to an individual as more audacious than catching rockets.
MS frames robots as compute nodes: 1 million robots in Austin averaging 1kW each would equal 1GW of interconnected compute in one city, and 10GW is posed as the next question.
MS expects the AI narrative to shift from jobs AI will take to jobs AI will make, tied to household and economic prosperity.
Elon Musk posted that hiring ex-NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang would be 'an honor'. MS raises the question of what that would mean for SPCX shares but gives no answer.
Investors with a positive view of further SpaceX/Tesla collaboration are hesitant to add exposure ahead of potential dilution risk.
Tesla (covered by Andrew Percoco) announced an incremental EUR3bn investment in Giga Berlin to expand Cybercab production by 2029, in contrast to headcount cuts at legacy OEMs.

If Musk is serious about 'tera' scale semiconductor fabrication, investors may see advancement of technologies such as Free Electron Lasers (FEL) versus today's EUV lithography. Musk posted 'FEL FTW' on August 6.
MS would not be surprised if China and US non-SPCX competitors double down on reusable architectures after Starship 15.
MS does not believe SPCX would license Falcon 9 architecture to other launch players.

MS argues Musk and SpaceX are not driven to build a world-leading neocloud or solely a frontier LLM. Its view is that connectivity, access to space and SI infrastructure combined with Tesla manufacturing lead to interconnected physical agents, which may drive net additions of millions of jobs.
Valuation: SPCX trades 3% above its $135 IPO offer price. Since early July MS 2027 EPS is up 80% and 2028 EPS up 60%.

At about $140, SPCX trades at 17.5x MS 2028 EPS (excluding tax benefits), assuming 8.3 GW versus Musk's guided 13 GW at end-2027 and an estimated 14 GW at end-2028, with revenue per watt falling from $34 in 1Q27 to $21 in FY28.
On Visible Alpha consensus ex tax benefits, SPCX trades at 11.2x 2028 P/E versus 16.2x for the S&P 500 (MSe).
Overweight rating and $300 price target (SOTP: Space $8, Connectivity $111, X & Grok $11, Enterprise AI $170). The Enterprise AI value carries a 50% discount for execution risk.

market_movers.rationale: MS keeps Overweight and a $300 SOTP target, saying SPCX looks cheap on 2028 P/E at about 17.5x MS estimates and 11.2x on consensus ex tax benefits. The muted reaction to Flight 15 reflects uncertainty over the AI/neocloud model, customer concentration and Tesla strategy.
Tesla announced an incremental EUR3bn investment in Giga Berlin to expand Cybercab production by 2029. The note is by Andrew Percoco, who covers Tesla.

sector_views.rationale: Industry View is Attractive. MS expects competitors to push on reusable architectures after Starship 15.

earnings_insights: MS EPS for SPCX: 2025 $(1.69) reported, 2026e $0.58, 2027e $3.95, 2028e $9.91 (MS ModelWare, consensus methodology). Refinitiv consensus EPS: 2026e $0.32, 2027e $3.48, 2028e $8.44.
Quarterly 2026 EPS, actual company-reported: Q1 $(0.84), Q2 $(0.09), Q3 $0.35. Q4 2026e is $0.44 (MS estimate). 2027e quarters: Q1 $0.86, Q2 $0.87, Q3 $0.98, Q4 $1.24.
MS 2028 EPS valuation excludes the tax benefit from a valuation allowance release.
risk_factors: Uncertainty in business model (AI/neocloud), customer concentration and strategy (Tesla).
Potential dilution risk from SpaceX/Tesla collaboration and greater funding needs.
Higher capex or cost per watt of compute, and longer time-to-power.
